players.name: Anki
players.what: Free open-source flashcard program with spaced repetition scheduling, now using FSRS as an optional scheduler.
players.learner: Self-directed adults, heavy in medical students and language learners
players.mechanism: User-made or shared flashcards reviewed at intervals set by SM-2 or FSRS
players.price: Desktop free; AnkiMobile iOS $24.99 one-time in the US store (checked 2026-09-08 by a third party)

efficacy.finding: Daily Anki users had median USMLE Step 1 of 238 vs 233.5 for non-daily users (P=.039); no difference on Step 2 (250 vs 251, P=.440). Authors say the link may reflect more total study time.
efficacy.design: Cross-sectional survey plus institutional score records, n=165 respondents of 887 (Step 1 scores for 99), University of Minnesota, 2023

players.name: AnkiHub
players.what: Collaborative deck platform for Anki that hosts the AnKing medical decks and is taking over Anki stewardship.
players.learner: Medical students and other exam cohorts using Anki
players.mechanism: Subscription sync of community-maintained shared decks into Anki, with crowd-suggested card edits
players.price: About $5 per month per a Feb 2026 Reddit snapshot; one guide lists Core about $6 and Premium about $10 per month. Official pricing page returned 404.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. Hits were unrelated genetics papers. The Anki row holds the one study of the underlying program.

players.name: Brainscape
players.what: Flashcard platform built on confidence-based repetition, with certified decks for exams.
players.learner: Students and professional exam takers
players.mechanism: Learner rates confidence 1 to 5 per card, which sets repeat frequency
players.price: Pro $19.99 per month; a Sept 2026 comparison lists $7.99 per month on a yearly web plan and $95.99 per year in app

efficacy.finding: Examined confidence-based repetition on two adults and states that very little systematic research exists on its effect on learning. Brainscape itself cites an unpublished Columbia experiment by its founder.
efficacy.design: Single-case style study, n=2 adults, knowledge quizzes (SUNY thesis)

players.name: Cerego
players.what: Adaptive learning platform that schedules retrieval practice for courses and workforce training.
players.learner: Higher-ed students and corporate or healthcare trainees
players.mechanism: Instructor-built item sets reviewed on a personalized spaced schedule with memory-strength analytics
players.price: Starting price $8.33 per month flat rate per Capterra 2026 listing

efficacy.finding: Company reports that learners with four reviews reach nearly 90% retention after 6 weeks, and cites partner results such as an 18% increase in student retention at University of Hawaii Manoa. Designs and controls are not described.
efficacy.design: Internal platform data and vendor case studies; a whitepaper references a K-12 peer-reviewed study that was not retrieved

players.name: Knowt
players.what: Free Quizlet alternative with AI flashcards from notes, PDFs and lectures, strong in US AP exam prep.
players.learner: US high school and college students
players.mechanism: AI-generated flashcards and practice tests, learn mode, spaced repetition option
players.price: Free Basic plan; Ultra annual from $12.49 per month per one tracker, $149.99 per year per another

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Memrise
players.what: Language vocabulary app that began as a spaced repetition mnemonic tool and now centers on video clips and AI chat.
players.learner: Casual adult language learners
players.mechanism: Spaced vocabulary review with native speaker video and AI conversation practice
players.price: US Pro about $8.99 per month, lifetime $139.99 (aggregator); another guide reports $14.99 to $24.99 per month

efficacy.finding: Memrise group scored higher than traditional teaching on immediate and delayed collocation tests; the abstract gives no effect size. The US pilot found no significant difference in character acquisition against paper flashcards (p > 0.05) and higher motivation in the app group.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment, two intact classes, n=75 Iranian intermediate EFL learners, immediate and delayed post-test (Esmaeili and Shahrokhi 2020). Second study: pilot with control, n=27 US middle school students of Chinese (Wang and Lam 2023).

players.name: Mnemosyne
players.what: Free open-source flashcard program that also collects opt-in review logs for memory research.
players.learner: Self-directed adults
players.mechanism: Flashcards scheduled by a modified SM-2 algorithm
players.price: Free

efficacy.finding: The project has gathered opt-in review data since 2006, and Andy Matuschak reports that the maintainer confirmed in 2023 that no serious analysis of it had been published.

players.name: Mochi
players.what: Markdown-based flashcard and notes app with spaced repetition, local-first.
players.learner: Developers, language learners, self-directed adults
players.mechanism: Markdown cards and templates reviewed on a spaced schedule; FSRS available as an option
players.price: Free forever with unlimited offline use; Pro $5 per month

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Noji
players.what: Mobile-first flashcard app formerly named Anki Pro, unaffiliated with Anki.
players.learner: Students and language learners on phones
players.mechanism: Flashcards with spaced repetition and a shared deck library
players.price: Free download, 3-day trial, then $29.99 per year (checked 2026-09-08 by a third party)

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Orbit
players.what: Andy Matuschak's experimental platform for embedding spaced repetition prompts inside essays, the mnemonic medium.
players.learner: Readers of technical essays; researchers of learning tools
players.mechanism: Author-written prompts embedded in text, then reviewed by email-prompted spaced sessions
players.price: Free

efficacy.finding: Readers who remembered an answer for 5 or more days had median accuracy of about 95% afterward. In the 2019 experiment, delayed readers fell 4 percentage points while controls rose 7. The author labels the data correlational and subject to survivorship.
efficacy.design: Observational reader data from Quantum Country plus one informal 2019 experiment delaying 8 questions by two weeks

players.name: Quizlet
players.what: Mass-market study set platform with flashcards, Learn mode, practice tests and AI study tools.
players.learner: High school and college students, about 13 to 24
players.mechanism: User-made study sets, self-testing modes; limited scheduling compared with SRS tools
players.price: Quizlet Plus $7.99 per month or $35.99 per year; Plus Unlimited $9.99 per month or $44.99 per year (third party read of quizlet.com/upgrade on 2026-09-08; official page returned 403)

efficacy.finding: Lap et al.: no significant difference in vocabulary gains between groups. Nguyen and Le: greater lexical gains with Quizlet; working memory and prior vocabulary predicted nothing. Two small studies, opposite results, no effect size in either abstract.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment, n=64 Vietnamese tenth graders, Quizlet against paper vocabulary notebooks, tests before, after and four weeks later (Lap et al. 2026). Second study: pretest-posttest with control, n=68 Vietnamese undergraduates (33 Quizlet, 35 control), five weeks (Nguyen and Le 2023).

players.name: RemNote
players.what: Note-taking app where notes become spaced repetition flashcards, with PDF annotation and a linked knowledge base.
players.learner: University students, med students, lifelong learners
players.mechanism: Outline notes with inline flashcard syntax, backlinks, spaced review
players.price: Free; Pro $8 per month or $96 per year; Pro with AI $18 per month or $216 per year

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: SuperMemo
players.what: The original spaced repetition software line, with a Windows desktop program and a separate SuperMemo.com course service.
players.learner: Dedicated autodidacts on Windows; language course buyers on SuperMemo.com
players.mechanism: Spaced repetition with the SM-18 algorithm plus incremental reading of imported texts
players.price: SuperMemo for Windows listed as a one-time $66 perpetual license on AlternativeTo (undated); SuperMemo.com says prices vary by country

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Vaia (StudySmarter)
players.what: Student study app with flashcards, notes, textbook solutions and AI study helpers; StudySmarter in DACH, Vaia in the US and Spain.
players.learner: School and university students
players.mechanism: User and publisher flashcards, study plans, summaries and quizzes

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. The one hit is a study-tips presentation with a similar name.

players.name: Babbel
players.what: Subscription language app with linguist-written courses, live classes and an AI speaking feature.
players.learner: Adult learners, 25 and up, travel and work motives
players.mechanism: Structured dialogue-based lessons with review manager and speech recognition
players.price: 12-month plan at $8.95 per month; lifetime $599 (2025 pricing review)

efficacy.finding: 59% of completers improved oral proficiency by at least one ACTFL sublevel; 69 to 70% among those studying at least 6 hours and 75 to 78% at 15 hours or more, depending on the report. No control group; 36% attrition.
efficacy.design: Pre-post, n=85 Michigan State undergraduates learning Spanish for 12 weeks, 54 completers, ACTFL OPIc (Loewen, Isbell, Sporn 2020, Foreign Language Annals)

players.name: Busuu
players.what: Language app with CEFR-aligned courses and peer correction from native speakers, owned by Chegg.
players.learner: Adult learners and corporate teams
players.mechanism: Structured lessons plus community feedback on writing and speaking exercises
players.price: Premium about $13.90 per month or $83.40 per year (Langoly); another 2026 review reports about $62.99 per year

efficacy.finding: Users needed an average of 22.5 hours over two months to cover one college semester of Spanish; all who studied at least 16 hours improved. A later company study cited by Chegg gives 13 hours.
efficacy.design: Pre-post, beginner Spanish learners over two months, WebCAPE and oral test; n reported as 144 in the executive summary and 196 on Busuu's page (Vesselinov and Grego 2016)

players.name: Cambly
players.what: On-demand English conversation practice with native-speaker tutors over video.
players.learner: Adult and child English learners, strong in Middle East and Asia
players.mechanism: Instant or scheduled video chats with tutors
players.price: Roughly $60 per month for 30 minutes weekly up to $200+ for unlimited (third-party estimate)

efficacy.finding: No significant difference between groups on the post-test and no significant pre to post gain in the Cambly group. Interviewees reported gains in confidence and motivation.
efficacy.design: Experiment with control group, n=28 EFL university students, four weeks of audio calls with native speakers, pre and post speaking tests plus interviews (Alshammary 2020).

players.name: Clozemaster
players.what: Fill-in-the-blank sentence drilling for vocabulary in context, built on Tatoeba sentences, for learners past the beginner stage.
players.learner: Intermediate self-directed learners
players.mechanism: Cloze deletion on frequency-ordered sentences with spaced review
players.price: Pro $12.99 per month or $69.99 per year; lifetime about $199; free tier 30 sentences a day

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Drops
players.what: Visual vocabulary game app with five-minute sessions, owned by Kahoot.
players.learner: Casual learners and travelers
players.mechanism: Swipe and match games pairing words with illustrations, with spaced review
players.price: In-app tiers of $9.99 and $69.99 listed on the US App Store, billing periods unlabeled

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. The one hit is unrelated.

players.name: Duolingo
players.what: Gamified mobile language app, the largest in the category, also offering math, music and chess.
players.learner: Casual learners of all ages
players.mechanism: Short gamified exercises, streaks, a half-life regression style review model, AI conversation in the top tier
players.price: Super $13.99 monthly or about $83.88 per year; Family $119.99 per year (third party read of duolingo.com, June 2026)

efficacy.finding: Learners who finished five units of Spanish or French scored comparably in reading and listening to students after four university semesters, reaching Intermediate Low reading and Novice High listening. Speaking and writing were not the focus.
efficacy.design: Cross-sectional, n=225 US learners with little prior knowledge who used only Duolingo, ACTFL reading and listening tests (Jiang et al. 2021, Foreign Language Annals)

players.name: ELSA Speak
players.what: AI pronunciation and speaking coach for English learners.
players.learner: Adult English learners, strong in Vietnam, India and Latin America
players.mechanism: Speech recognition scores pronunciation at the sound level and gives corrective drills

efficacy.finding: Company claims 27 hours with ELSA equals an American university ESL speaking course, and over 95% accuracy in pronunciation error detection.
efficacy.design: Self-reported website claim, design not found

players.name: italki
players.what: Marketplace for one-to-one online language lessons with freelance teachers.
players.learner: Adult learners wanting live tutoring
players.mechanism: Paid live video lessons; teachers set price and schedule
players.price: About $5 to $30 per lesson depending on teacher

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Lingoda
players.what: Online language school with small-group and private live classes on a CEFR curriculum.
players.learner: Adult learners, relocation and career motives
players.mechanism: Scheduled live classes with teachers, 24 hours a day
players.price: 5 group classes $39.99, 12 for $85.99, 20 for $143.99, 40 for $242.99 per 4 weeks (Aug 2026 review); other reviews cite $99 for 8

efficacy.finding: Bundle group scored 74.71 on the final test against 65.9 for control. The design cannot separate Lingoda from the other three apps.
efficacy.design: Controlled comparison, n=140 Chinese college students at B2 or below (70 per group); the treatment was a bundle of Busuu, Lingoda, LinguaLeo and BBC Learning English (Gou 2023).

players.name: LingoDeer
players.what: Grammar-focused language app strongest in Japanese, Korean and Chinese.
players.learner: Adult learners of Asian languages
players.mechanism: Structured grammar lessons with explanations, drills and review
players.price: $14.99 monthly, $39.99 quarterly, $95.99 annual (promo from $159.99); 3-year plan $189.99

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: LingQ
players.what: Reading and listening platform where learners import content and track known words, founded by Steve Kaufmann.
players.learner: Self-directed adult learners, intermediate and up
players.mechanism: Extensive reading and listening with click-to-save words that feed an SRS review
players.price: Premium $14.99 per month or $119.99 per year; Premium Plus $41.99 per month; lifetime $229 per language

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Pimsleur
players.what: Audio-first language courses built on graduated interval recall, published by Simon and Schuster.
players.learner: Adult commuters and travelers
players.mechanism: 30-minute audio lessons prompting spoken recall at expanding intervals
players.price: Premium about $19.95 per month; All Access about $20.95 per month, annual $164.95 on renewal (aggregators citing April 2026 checks)

efficacy.finding: No efficacy study of this product surfaced in this session's searches.

players.name: Preply
players.what: Tutoring marketplace focused on languages, with AI lesson tools layered on human tutors.
players.learner: Adult learners and corporate teams
players.mechanism: Recurring one-to-one video lessons with matched tutors

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Rosetta Stone
players.what: Immersion-style language software, the legacy brand in the category, now part of IXL Learning.
players.learner: Adult consumers, schools and enterprises
players.mechanism: Picture-word association without translation, speech recognition
players.price: Lifetime all-languages around $199, promoted at $149 to $179 against a $399 list (aggregators)

efficacy.finding: Severe attrition made outcome assessment nearly impossible; the author concluded more resource-intensive training is likely more effective than software self-study.
efficacy.design: Observational self-study trial, n=150 US government employees, absolute beginners (Nielson 2011, Language Learning and Technology)

players.name: Speak
players.what: AI speaking tutor app backed by the OpenAI Startup Fund, strongest in Korea and expanding to more languages.
players.learner: Adult English and Spanish learners who want speaking practice
players.mechanism: Spoken role-play with an AI tutor and speech recognition feedback
players.price: Premium $17.99 per month or $83.99 per year; Premium Plus $39.99 per month or $164.99 per year (July 2026)

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: ALEKS (McGraw Hill)
players.what: Adaptive math and chemistry courseware that maps what a student knows and assigns the topics they are ready to learn.
players.learner: K-12 and college students, mostly through schools
players.mechanism: Knowledge space theory assessment places the learner, then mastery practice on ready-to-learn topics with periodic reassessment.
players.price: Consumer: $19.95 for 1 month, $49.95 for 3 months, $99.95 for 6 months, $179.95 for 12 months. Page undated.

efficacy.finding: ALEKS performed as well as traditional classroom teaching. Sun et al. report Hedges g = 0.05 overall and g = 0.43 when ALEKS supplements instruction.
efficacy.design: Meta-analysis of 15 studies and 24 samples (Fang, Ren, Hu, Graesser 2019); second meta-analysis of 33 studies (Sun et al. 2021)

players.name: Amira Learning
players.what: Speech-recognition reading tutor that listens to children read aloud, assesses and coaches.
players.learner: K-5 readers through schools
players.mechanism: Oral reading with automatic speech recognition, micro-interventions on errors, and screening assessment.

efficacy.finding: Evidence for ESSA average effect size +0.15, rated moderate. Utah high-use students: 0.41 in grade 1, 0.45 in grade 2, 0.25 in grade 3. Texas 2024-25 vendor study: 0.26 in kindergarten, 0.06 in grade 1.
efficacy.design: Evidence for ESSA lists 2 studies with 15,602 students in grades K-4; Utah 2022-23 evaluation by the Evaluation and Training Institute

players.name: Art of Problem Solving and Beast Academy
players.what: Advanced math curriculum for strong students: books, online classes, a forum, and the Beast Academy comic-based elementary program.
players.learner: Ages 6 to 18, math-talented students and their families
players.mechanism: Hard problem sequences with worked solutions, live text-based classes, and an adaptive online practice platform for elementary grades.
players.price: Beast Academy Online $99.99 per year or $15.99 per month for the first student; $64.99 per year for each sibling

efficacy.finding: No efficacy study found.
efficacy.design: Searched; no outcome study surfaced

players.name: Area9 Lyceum (Rhapsode)
players.what: Adaptive learning platform for corporate, medical and higher education training.
players.learner: Employees, clinicians, students via institutions
players.mechanism: Confidence-rated self-assessment probes that route learners to content on their gaps until proficiency.

efficacy.finding: No independent evaluation found.
efficacy.design: Company claims training time cut in half

players.name: ASSISTments
players.what: Free online math homework tool that gives students immediate feedback and gives teachers reports.
players.learner: Middle school math students and teachers
players.mechanism: Students do assigned problems with instant correctness feedback and hints; teachers use the report to plan the next lesson.
players.price: Free

efficacy.finding: Maine: g = 0.18, about 60 percent of a typical annual gain. North Carolina: sustained effect at end of eighth grade, about 31 percent of typical annual gain.
efficacy.design: Two cluster RCTs run by SRI and WestEd: Maine, 43 to 46 schools and about 2,850 to 3,050 seventh graders (Roschelle et al. 2016); North Carolina replication, 63 schools and 9,073 seventh graders

players.name: Brilliant
players.what: Interactive problem-based courses in math, science, data and computer science.
players.learner: Teens and adults learning for interest or career
players.mechanism: Short interactive puzzles and visual explorations in sequenced courses with streaks.
players.price: Brilliant states Premium costs $240 a year or $30 month to month in the United States; third-party sites list $149.88 or $161.88 a year

efficacy.finding: No published study of Brilliant outcomes found.
efficacy.design: Marketing cites unnamed research that interactive learning is 6x more effective than lecture video

players.name: Carnegie Learning MATHia
players.what: Intelligent tutoring software for middle and high school math, descended from Cognitive Tutor.
players.learner: Grades 6-12 students through districts
players.mechanism: Step-level model tracing with hints and skill mastery tracking on multi-step problems.
players.price: MATHiaFlex supplemental product $22 to $27 per student per year (third-party review site)

efficacy.finding: No effect in the first year. High school students in the second year outperformed controls by about 0.2 SD. Evidence for ESSA lists +0.22 for the second cohort and +0.07 for the first.
efficacy.design: RAND cluster RCT of Cognitive Tutor Algebra I in 7 states (Pane et al. 2014), IES-funded

players.name: DreamBox (Discovery Education)
players.what: Adaptive K-8 math and reading programs sold to schools.
players.learner: K-8 students through districts
players.mechanism: Game-like lessons that adapt sequence and difficulty to each response.

efficacy.finding: More time on DreamBox tracked with larger gains, and causal evidence was encouraging but mixed. Students averaged 35 to 44 minutes a week against a recommended 60 to 90.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experimental and correlational, about 3,000 students grades 3 to 5 in Howard County MD and Rocketship CA, 2013-2015

players.name: IXL
players.what: Skill-by-skill practice platform for math, language arts, science and social studies.
players.learner: PreK-12 students, schools and families
players.mechanism: Thousands of narrow skills with adaptive question difficulty, a SmartScore mastery number and a diagnostic.
players.price: Family membership about $9.95 per month for one subject, $19.95 for core subjects, $159 per year (third-party page, 2026)

efficacy.finding: IXL Math students scored about 10 points higher on Star Math than controls (ESSA Tier 1). Oklahoma schools showed about 4 percentage points more proficiency (Tier 2).
efficacy.design: Cluster RCT, grades 3 to 5, Holland Public Schools Michigan, spring 2023, run by Johns Hopkins CRRE; SRI reviewed a quasi-experimental study of 179 Oklahoma schools

players.name: Khan Academy
players.what: Free nonprofit library of video lessons and mastery practice across K-12 and early college subjects.
players.learner: K-12 students, teachers, adult learners
players.mechanism: Short videos plus practice exercises with mastery levels by skill and course.
players.price: Free

efficacy.finding: Use of 30 or more minutes per week was associated with about 20 percent greater than expected gains, effect size 0.36. Khan Academy also lists a 2026 PNAS study reporting 0.09 to 0.18 SD gains on MAP Growth.
efficacy.design: Correlational study of about 350,000 students in grades 3 to 8, 2022-23, against MAP Growth norms

players.name: Khanmigo (Khan Academy)
players.what: AI tutor and teaching assistant built into Khan Academy.
players.learner: K-12 students, parents, teachers
players.mechanism: Chat tutor that asks guiding questions tied to Khan Academy exercises; lesson planning tools for teachers.
players.price: Learners and parents $4 per month or $44 per year; teachers free; districts request pricing

efficacy.finding: No study of Khanmigo itself found in this session.
efficacy.design: Searched for a randomized or independent evaluation of Khanmigo

players.name: Knewton Alta (Wiley)
players.what: Adaptive college courseware for math, statistics, chemistry and economics built on open educational resources.
players.learner: US college students in intro courses
players.mechanism: Mastery-based assignments that insert remediation on prerequisite gaps.
players.price: $39.95 per course, $9.95 per month, or $79.95 Altapass for a subject area up to two years (2018-2019 figures)

efficacy.finding: Students who finished Alta assignments scored 22 percent better on tests. Struggling students rose from 40 to 78 percent correct.
efficacy.design: Knewton fall 2018 usage analysis; Johns Hopkins CRRE study commissioned by Knewton (findings not visible in snippet)

players.name: Math Academy
players.what: Online math program from 4th grade through university level that picks every task for the student.
players.learner: Self-learners, homeschoolers and adults, 4th grade math through university courses
players.mechanism: Diagnostic builds a custom course on a knowledge graph; mastery learning with spaced repetition scheduled across the graph.
players.price: $49 per month per student, labeled beta pricing, 30-day money-back guarantee

efficacy.finding: No independent study found. Search returned only studies of the unrelated My Math Academy product.
efficacy.design: Site cites testimonials and a claim of learning at 4X the speed of a traditional class

players.name: My Math Academy (Age of Learning)
players.what: Game-based adaptive math program for early grades from the maker of ABCmouse.
players.learner: PreK to grade 2 students through schools
players.mechanism: Adaptive games sequenced on a map of early math skills.

efficacy.finding: Trial under way in the sources found; no result recorded.
efficacy.design: IES-funded cluster RCT by WestEd assigning 66 elementary schools; results not found. Vendor briefs use matched comparison designs.

players.name: Prodigy
players.what: Free role-playing game where math and English questions power battles.
players.learner: Grades 1-8 students at school and home
players.mechanism: Adaptive curriculum-aligned questions embedded in game play.
players.price: Premium membership reported at $59 to $100 per year per child (2021 coverage)

efficacy.finding: More Prodigy use correlated with larger math gains. Critics at NEPC say this does not support causal claims.
efficacy.design: Correlational study by Johns Hopkins CRRE, 2019, commissioned by Prodigy; 2025 company white papers compare high-usage schools to state averages

players.name: Squirrel AI Learning
players.what: Chinese adaptive tutoring system delivered through learning centers and tablets.
players.learner: K-12 students in China
players.mechanism: Fine-grained knowledge point map with diagnostic testing and adaptive sequencing of lessons and practice.

efficacy.finding: Students assigned to Squirrel AI made larger math test gains than peers taught by expert teachers. Effect sizes not shown in the snippet.
efficacy.design: Two randomized efficacy studies of eighth graders in two Chinese provinces, written up with SRI researchers and Squirrel AI staff

players.name: Synthesis Tutor
players.what: Tablet-first math tutor for children that grew out of the Ad Astra school at SpaceX.
players.learner: Children ages 5 to 11
players.mechanism: Scripted interactive lessons with manipulatives and micro-assessments inside each lesson.
players.price: Family plan (up to 7 kids) $119 per year or $29 per month, lifetime $1,499; individual $29 per month billed annually or $35 monthly, lifetime $999

efficacy.finding: No efficacy study found.
efficacy.design: Searched for outcome studies

players.name: Coursera
players.what: Largest MOOC marketplace for university and industry courses, certificates and degrees; merged with Udemy in May 2026.
players.learner: Adults seeking career skills and credentials; enterprises, universities
players.mechanism: Video lectures, auto-graded quizzes and projects on a cohort or self-paced schedule, ending in a certificate.
players.price: Coursera Plus $59 per month or $399 per year in the US (2024-2025 third-party sources)

efficacy.finding: Completion rates did not improve over six years. Inside Higher Ed reports 3.13 percent of all participants completed (year truncated in the snippet). More than half of registrants never opened the courseware. Second-year retention fell from 38 percent to 7 percent.
efficacy.design: Observational analysis of edX data from Harvard and MIT: 565 course runs, nearly 13 million registrations, more than 5.6 million learners, 2013-14 to 2017-18 (Reich and Ruiperez-Valiente, Science 2019)

players.name: Domestika
players.what: Creative course marketplace and community with strong Spanish and Portuguese language reach.
players.learner: Adult creatives worldwide
players.mechanism: Produced video courses by working creatives with a final project and community feedback.
players.price: Domestika Plus $164.50 for the first year, renewing at $329 (2026 third-party guide)

efficacy.finding: No efficacy study found.
efficacy.design: Searched; none surfaced

players.name: edX and 2U
players.what: MOOC platform founded by Harvard and MIT, owned since 2021 by online program manager 2U.
players.learner: Adults seeking university courses, certificates, boot camps and online degrees
players.mechanism: University video courses with graded assignments; paid verified track for a certificate.
players.price: Free to audit; verified certificates roughly $50 to $300 per course (third-party review sites)

efficacy.finding: Completion rates did not improve over six years. Inside Higher Ed reports 3.13 percent of all participants completed (year truncated in the snippet). More than half of registrants never opened the courseware. Second-year retention fell from 38 percent to 7 percent.
efficacy.design: Observational analysis of edX data from Harvard and MIT: 565 course runs, nearly 13 million registrations, more than 5.6 million learners, 2013-14 to 2017-18 (Reich and Ruiperez-Valiente, Science 2019)

players.name: FutureLearn
players.what: UK MOOC platform founded by the Open University, owned by Global University Systems since November 2022.
players.learner: Adult learners, strongest in the UK and Commonwealth
players.mechanism: Short weekly-step courses with discussion threads on each step.
players.price: Unlimited listed at $27.99 per month or $279.99 per year on a 2026 third-party page; official 2019 launch price was 189 pounds a year

efficacy.finding: No FutureLearn-specific study found.
efficacy.design: Searched; none surfaced

players.name: The Great Courses Plus (formerly Wondrium)

efficacy.design: Content analysis: four AI platforms asked to reproduce four PRISMA-based glaucoma systematic reviews (Meliante et al. 2025, JMIR AI).

players.name: Consensus
players.what: AI search engine that answers questions from peer-reviewed papers with cited summaries.
players.learner: Students, researchers and clinicians
players.mechanism: Search over a paper index, LLM summaries per paper and a synthesized answer with citations.
players.price: Pricing page names Individual and Team and Enterprise plans and showed no figures when fetched. One comparison site lists a paid plan from $9.

efficacy.finding: ChatGPT-5 returned the highest share of relevant articles (90%); performance across tools was heterogeneous. The rapid review found reported use of Consensus in the literature low. Measures retrieval; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Blinded comparison of ChatGPT-5, Elicit, Consensus, Scite and PubMed on four cardiology topics, three expert raters, two gold standards (Di Febo et al. 2026, European Heart Journal Digital Health). Also a rapid review of 10 papers on the app (Apata et al. 2025).

players.name: Elicit
players.what: AI research assistant that searches papers, screens them and extracts data into tables for literature and systematic reviews.
players.learner: Researchers running literature reviews, in academia, pharma and policy
players.mechanism: Semantic search over a paper corpus, LLM screening against criteria, LLM extraction into table columns with supporting quotes, generated research reports.
players.price: Basic free. Pro $49/user/month or $588/year. Scale $169/user/month or $2,028/year. Enterprise custom. Pro screens up to 5,000 papers and extracts from up to 135 sources per report.

efficacy.finding: Elicit extracted 'more' data than the human in 29.3% of cases, 'equal' in 20.7%, 'partially equal' in 45.7%, 'deviating' in 4.3%. Authors conclude human verification is needed.
efficacy.design: Bianchi, Hirt, Vogt, Vetsch 2025, Cochrane Evidence Synthesis and Methods 3(4):e70033. Elicit extraction compared with a human reviewer on 20 randomized controlled trials across seven variables.

players.name: EndNote (Clarivate)
players.what: Commercial desktop reference manager from Clarivate.
players.learner: Academics and institutions, strong in medicine and systematic reviews
players.mechanism: Desktop library of references and PDFs, Cite While You Write plugin, sync to EndNote web.
players.price: EndNote 2025: $275 full licence, $150 student, $125 upgrade; promotional $234, $128, $106 in some page snapshots. Site licences quoted privately.

efficacy.finding: EndNote retrieved 47% of available full texts against 52% for Zotero; 99% of retrieved files were correct. Deduplication: sensitivity 0.939, specificity 1.000, about 40 minutes per dataset. Measures tool accuracy; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Full-text retrieval test on 1,000 records from four evidence syntheses, EndNote 20 against Zotero 6 (Fulbright and Evans 2024, JMLA). Also a deduplication crossover on 1,564 synthetic records with 428 duplicates (Sagar et al. 2025, preprint).

players.name: Google Scholar
players.what: Free academic search engine from Google, with an experimental AI mode called Scholar Labs.
players.learner: Everyone who searches the scholarly literature
players.mechanism: Keyword search over crawled scholarly documents ranked with citation counts; cited-by links, alerts, author profiles, personal library.

efficacy.finding: Bramer: coverage 97.2%, recall 72.8% against 81.6% for Embase with MEDLINE; the 1,000-result cap limits recall. Gusenbauer: unsuitable as the principal system for evidence synthesis. Gehanno: all 738 studies were present. Measures retrieval; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Prospective comparison on 4,795 included references from 120 systematic reviews (Bramer et al. 2016). Also a query-based test of 28 academic search systems (Gusenbauer and Haddaway 2020) and a coverage check on 738 studies from 29 reviews (Gehanno et al. 2013).

players.name: Heptabase
players.what: Visual note-taking tool that arranges note cards on whiteboards for learning and research on complex topics.
players.learner: Students, researchers and self-directed learners
players.mechanism: Cards placed and connected on whiteboards, PDF highlights, YouTube transcripts, AI agent and AI tutor over the user's material.
players.price: Pro $8.99/month, Premium $17.99/month, Premium+ $53.99/month; third-party profile says these are yearly-billing rates and monthly is $11.99, $23.99, $71.99.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Litmaps
players.what: Literature mapping tool that visualizes citation networks and sends alerts on new related papers. New Zealand company that also owns ResearchRabbit.
players.learner: Students and researchers doing literature reviews
players.mechanism: Seed-based search over the citation graph, visual maps, monitoring alerts.
players.price: Free: 2 Litmaps, 100 articles per map. Pro $10/month monthly or $120/year, academic email required. Team and Enterprise by quote.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. Hits name the tool in passing inside reviews; none evaluates it.

players.name: Logseq
players.what: Open-source outliner for linked notes, with a file-based version and a newer database version in beta.
players.learner: Privacy-minded knowledge workers, researchers and students
players.mechanism: Outliner blocks with links and queries; built-in flashcards (unverified this session).
players.price: App free. Sync about $5/month or $4.17/month billed annually per several third-party sources; one source says sync is a beta perk for Open Collective donors at $5 to $15 a month.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Mendeley (Elsevier)
players.what: Reference manager with cloud library, Word plugin and an AI Reading Assistant, owned by Elsevier.
players.learner: Students and academics, often through institutional Elsevier agreements
players.mechanism: Web importer and desktop app sync a PDF library to Elsevier cloud; citation plugin; AI question answering over a paper or the library.
players.price: Free: 2 GB and 5 Reading Assistant questions. Plus $4.99/month or $55/year, 5 GB. Pro $9.99/month or $110/year, 10 GB. Max $14.99/month or $165/year, unlimited storage.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. A refined title search returned one altmetrics study; no test of the tool or of learning.

players.name: Notion
players.what: All-in-one workspace of documents, wikis and databases with built-in AI agents.
players.learner: Teams and individuals; students use it for notes and course planning
players.mechanism: Block-based pages and relational databases in the cloud; AI agent answers and writes across the workspace.
players.price: Free $0. Plus $10 per member/month. Business $20 per member/month. Enterprise custom. Custom Agents $10 per 1,000 monthly credits. Yearly billing saves up to 20%.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. Hits use the common word notion; none concerns the app.

players.name: Obsidian
players.what: Note-taking app that works on a folder of Markdown files with links between notes and a large plugin ecosystem.
players.learner: Knowledge workers, writers, researchers and students building personal knowledge bases
players.mechanism: Linked plain-text notes, backlinks, graph view, community plugins.
players.price: App free. Sync $4/user/month annual or $5 monthly. Publish $8/site/month annual or $10 monthly. Catalyst $25 one-time. Commercial $50/user/year.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. Two hits describe workflows built on Obsidian; neither measures an outcome.

players.name: OpenAlex (OurResearch)
players.what: Open index of scholarly works, authors, institutions and citations, run by a nonprofit, used as a data layer by other tools.
players.learner: Bibliometricians, tool builders, libraries; agents through the API
players.mechanism: Aggregated scholarly graph served through an API and a free full snapshot.
players.price: Free: $1 of API usage per day. Pay as you go in $1 increments. Member $5,000/year with $20/day budget. Member+ $10,000/year with $100/day. Partner from $20,000/year. Full snapshot free.

efficacy.finding: OpenAlex covered 98.6%, the highest of four, and missed no low-risk-of-bias article. A second study found author identifiers missing on 30.2% and affiliations on 69% of addiction dataset records (Melero-Fuentes et al. 2026). Measures coverage; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Coverage test: articles included in the 2023 international PCOS guidelines retrieved by identifier from four databases (Rajit et al. 2025, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology).

players.name: Paperpile
players.what: Web-based reference manager built around Google Docs and Google Drive.
players.learner: Academics and students who write in Google Docs
players.mechanism: Browser extension collects papers, PDFs stored in the user's Google Drive, citation add-on for Google Docs and Word.
players.price: Regular $4.15/month and Expert $5.75/month, billed annually, shown alongside $8.30 and $11.50. 50% academic discount. Enterprise custom. 30-day trial, no free tier.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. One descriptive overview of reference managers; no evaluation.

players.name: Perplexity and Deep Research tools
players.what: General AI answer engines and multi-step research agents that browse sources and write cited reports. One row for Perplexity and the deep research modes of the large chat assistants.
players.learner: General public, students and knowledge workers
players.mechanism: LLM plans queries, retrieves web pages or papers, writes an answer with inline citations.
players.price: Perplexity Pro $20/month, Max $200/month. No separate Deep Research price found.

efficacy.finding: The tools together gave incorrect answers to more than 60 percent of queries. Perplexity 37 percent incorrect, Grok 3 94 percent. ChatGPT Search misidentified 134 of 200 articles.
efficacy.design: Tow Center for Digital Journalism, Columbia, published 2025-03-06. Eight AI search tools, 200 news articles from 20 publishers, 1,600 queries asking each tool to identify headline, publisher, date and URL from an excerpt. Tests run February 2025.

players.name: Readwise and Reader
players.what: Highlight aggregator that resurfaces saved highlights in a Daily Review, plus Reader, a read-it-later app for articles, PDFs, EPUBs, feeds and video.
players.learner: Heavy readers, knowledge workers and researchers
players.mechanism: Syncs highlights from Kindle and other sources, resurfaces them daily by weighted sampling, converts chosen highlights into Mastery flashcards with a recall-probability half-life.
players.price: Lite $5.59/month billed annually, Daily Review and library. Full $9.99/month billed annually ($119.88) or $12.99 monthly, adds Reader and exports. 50% academic discount by email.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: ResearchRabbit
players.what: Citation-network discovery tool that grows a collection of papers from seed articles, owned by Litmaps since 2025.
players.learner: Students and researchers mapping a field
players.mechanism: Seed papers expand through citation and similarity links into visual maps and recommendations.
players.price: Free forever with up to 50 seed articles. RR+ $10/month annual or $12.5/month monthly, up to 300 seed articles. Institution by quote. Discounts in 100+ countries.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. Hits name the tool in passing or concern rabbits; none evaluates it.

players.name: Roam Research
players.what: Outliner with bidirectional links and block references, the product that popularized networked note-taking.
players.learner: Researchers, writers and knowledge workers
players.mechanism: Daily notes, block-level links and references, graph database in the cloud.
players.price: Pro $15/month. Believer $500 for a multi-year term, shown as $41.67/month by CostBench. No free plan as of August 2026.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Scholarcy
players.what: AI summarizer that turns papers and chapters into structured summary flashcards.
players.learner: Students and researchers skimming many papers
players.mechanism: Extracts key claims, methods and references from a document into a fixed summary card layout.
players.price: Third-party sources: free tier about 1 summary per day; Plus $9.99/month or $90/year; another lists $7.99/month. Institutional from about GBP 6,000 or $8,000 a year.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. One overview article names the tool; no evaluation.

players.name: SciSpace (formerly Typeset)
players.what: AI research workspace with paper search, chat with PDF, literature review tables and writing tools.
players.learner: Students and researchers
players.mechanism: LLM question answering over uploaded or indexed papers, extraction tables, explain-this-passage reader.
players.price: Third-party sources conflict: Premium $12/month annual with a free tier (top50aitools); Premium $20/month annual, Advanced $90, Max $200, no free tier (CostBench); Capterra lists $20 starting price and a free version.

efficacy.finding: The SciSpace arm was stopped for futility after data export failures. Elicit found 33.3% of relevant publications and Nested Knowledge 78.8%. Measures tool accuracy; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Replication of three systematic reviews with Elicit, SciSpace and Nested Knowledge (Wong et al. 2026, preprint).

players.name: Scite (Research Solutions)
players.what: Citation index that shows the sentence where a paper is cited and labels it as supporting, contrasting or mentioning, plus an AI assistant.
players.learner: Researchers, students, publishers and corporate R&D
players.mechanism: Full-text citation extraction, classifier labels each citation statement, search and assistant answer with those citations.
players.price: Basic $20/month and Pro $50/month billed yearly, 7-day trial. Team $250/month with 8 seats, $50 per extra seat. Enterprise custom.

efficacy.finding: ChatGPT-5 returned the highest share of relevant articles (90%); the abstract gives no Scite figure. Measures retrieval; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Blinded comparison of ChatGPT-5, Elicit, Consensus, Scite and PubMed on four cardiology topics, three expert raters (Di Febo et al. 2026).

players.name: Semantic Scholar (Ai2)
players.what: Free AI-driven academic search engine and open scholarly graph from the Allen Institute for AI.
players.learner: Researchers and students; developers through the API
players.mechanism: Paper index with citation graph, paper recommendations, machine-generated summaries, public API and datasets.
players.price: Free. The librarian page says it 'is and always will be free and open for all to use'.

efficacy.finding: Semantic Scholar covered 98.3%, OpenAlex 98.6%, Embase 96.8%, PubMed 93.0%. Measures coverage; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Coverage test: articles included in the 2023 international PCOS guidelines retrieved by identifier from four databases (Rajit et al. 2025, Journal of Clinical Epidemiology).

players.name: Tana
players.what: AI-native workspace built on an outliner with typed nodes called supertags, now centred on meetings and voice capture.
players.learner: Knowledge workers and teams
players.mechanism: Outline nodes tagged into structured objects on a knowledge graph; AI meeting agent, transcripts and queries.
players.price: Free $0 with 5 hosted meetings a month and 50 AI queries. Pro $20/user/month early-bird, shown alongside $30. Business custom, billed yearly.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Undermind
players.what: AI search agent that runs a multi-step literature search and returns a ranked report of relevant papers.
players.learner: Scientists and R&D teams with complex search questions
players.mechanism: Candidate retrieval by embeddings and citations, LLM relevance classification of each paper, adaptive follow-up search, estimate of how complete the search is.
players.price: Free $0. Pro $16/month billed annually. Team $15 per person per month billed annually. Enterprise custom. Observed August 2026 as academic annual pricing.

efficacy.finding: Claims 10x more relevant results than the first 5 pages of Google Scholar for the median query, about 1 in 10 Google Scholar top hits highly relevant, Undermind missing under 3% of Google Scholar's highly relevant results, classifier accuracy about 98%.
efficacy.design: Whitepaper by founders Thomas Hartke and Joshua Ramette, dated 2024-01-05. About 300 user queries from late 2023, Undermind over 2.3 million arXiv full texts compared with the first page of Google Scholar results for 5 keyword rephrasings per query; relevance of both judged by Undermind's own GPT-4 classifier.

players.name: Zotero
players.what: Reference manager that collects, organizes, annotates and cites papers, run by the nonprofit Digital Scholar.
players.learner: Students, academics and independent researchers
players.mechanism: Browser connector saves metadata and PDFs into a local library; built-in PDF reader with annotations; word processor plugins insert citations.
players.price: Software free. Storage: 300 MB free, 2 GB $20/year, 6 GB $60/year, Unlimited $120/year. Lab from $450 for up to 15 users. Institution $2,315 for the first 500 FTE plus $0.46 per additional FTE.

efficacy.finding: Zotero retrieved 52% of available full texts against 47% for EndNote and ran 2 minutes 15 seconds faster. Two classroom reports describe Zotero annotation activities with no comparison group. Measures tool accuracy; no learning outcome.
efficacy.design: Full-text retrieval test on 1,000 records from four evidence syntheses, Zotero 6 against EndNote 20, University of York subscriptions (Fulbright and Evans 2024, JMLA).

players.name: Age of Learning (ABCmouse)
players.what: Maker of the ABCmouse early-learning subscription for ages 2 to 8, Adventure Academy for ages 8 to 13, and the school products My Math Academy and My Reading Academy.
players.learner: Children aged 2 to 13 and their parents; schools for the Academy products
players.mechanism: Sequenced games, books, songs and puzzles along a learning path; the Academy products add adaptive mastery sequencing

efficacy.finding: ABCmouse study concluded the program 'improved school readiness'. My Math Academy study found gains for kindergarten and first-grade students, largest for children with lower starting math knowledge. No effect sizes were read.
efficacy.design: Wikipedia cites a two-year longitudinal study in the Journal of Applied Research on Children (2016) and a study of My Math Academy in the Early Childhood Education Journal (2023); it attributes several randomized trials to the company's own research page

players.name: Amplify
players.what: K-12 core curriculum and assessment publisher: Amplify CKLA for reading, Amplify Science, Desmos Math, and mCLASS early-literacy assessment.
players.learner: K-8 students; the buyer is the district
players.mechanism: Print and digital core curriculum with teacher-led lessons, plus one-to-one mCLASS reading assessment and intervention

efficacy.finding: CKLA students scored higher at post-test on researcher-built measures of taught vocabulary, science and social studies and on a standardized expressive vocabulary measure. Amplify says the study meets ESSA Tier I. No effect size appeared in the search results and the Evidence for ESSA listing was not opened.
efficacy.design: Randomized comparison of CKLA Knowledge classrooms against business-as-usual classrooms, by Sonia Cabell and Hyejin Hwang; sample size not shown in the snippet

players.name: Blackboard (Anthology)
players.what: Higher-education and K-12 learning management system. Its parent Anthology filed for Chapter 11 on 2025-09-29 and the teaching and learning unit is emerging under the Blackboard name.
players.learner: College and K-12 students and instructors; the buyer is the institution
players.mechanism: Course shells, assignments, gradebook, Ally accessibility checks

efficacy.finding: Breakout group scored higher on cognitive achievement and held it one month later. The study tests collaborative breakout groups; both arms used Blackboard.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment, n=40 students randomly assigned 20 and 20; Blackboard Collaborate breakout groups against online lectures on the same platform (Rakha 2023).

players.name: Canvas (Instructure)
players.what: Cloud learning management system for higher education and K-12, owned by Instructure, which KKR and Dragoneer took private in November 2024.
players.learner: College students, K-12 students, and their instructors; the buyer is the institution
players.mechanism: Course shells with modules, assignments, quizzes, gradebook, and LTI integrations with third-party tools
players.price: No public price. The Canvas page says the product comes in three tiers and gives no dollar amounts.

efficacy.finding: No difference in number of posts or replies; word count per post favoured Reddit in one course (r = 0.44) and Canvas in the other (r = 0.47). Outcome is engagement; no learning measure.
efficacy.design: Non-randomized controlled trial, n=77 undergraduates in two psychology courses, discussion boards on Canvas against Reddit (Neff and Mischel 2023).

players.name: ClassDojo
players.what: Classroom communication and behavior-points app for elementary schools, free for teachers and funded by a family subscription.
players.learner: Elementary students, their teachers and parents
players.mechanism: Teacher awards points for behaviors, shares photos and messages with families; paid tier adds home features
players.price: ClassDojo Plus price is not shown on the Plus page; it says plans vary and offers a 7-day free trial.

efficacy.finding: Post-test scores showed a statistically significant rise; attendance and task completion were high. No control group.
efficacy.design: One-group pretest-posttest, n=30 Year 4 pupils learning Mandarin as a second language, Malaysia (Ng and Alias 2022).

players.name: D2L Brightspace
players.what: Learning management system for higher education, K-12 and corporate training from D2L, listed on the Toronto Stock Exchange since November 2021.
players.learner: College and K-12 students, corporate learners; the buyer is the institution
players.mechanism: Course shells, release conditions, competency tracking, gradebook

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Google Classroom
players.what: Free assignment and class-management layer on top of Google Workspace for Education.
players.learner: K-12 students and teachers, some higher education
players.mechanism: Class streams, assignments tied to Docs and Drive, grading, guardian summaries
players.price: Education Fundamentals is free. Standard and Plus are quote-based per a third-party review site; no per-student price was found.

efficacy.finding: Project model with Google Classroom gave a creative-thinking gain score of 0.47; the teaching model changes with the platform. Nigerian study: higher engagement scores with Google Classroom; engagement outcome only.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment, n=86 Grade XI science students, Indonesia, three teaching models, one assisted by Google Classroom (Jumadi et al. 2021). Second study: n=118 Nigerian undergraduates, Google Classroom against WhatsApp instruction (Ukala and Okoli 2025).

players.name: Curriculum Associates i-Ready
players.what: Adaptive diagnostic plus online lessons in reading and math for K-8, sold with the i-Ready Classroom Mathematics core curriculum.
players.learner: K-8 students; the buyer is the district
players.mechanism: Computer-adaptive diagnostic three times a year places each student into a sequence of online lessons

efficacy.finding: All three rated moderate. Average effect sizes: +0.23 math, +0.12 reading, +0.10 for i-Ready Classroom Mathematics, the last measured on the vendor's own i-Ready Diagnostic.
efficacy.design: Evidence for ESSA review. Personalized Instruction Math: 1 study, 2,256 students. Personalized Instruction Reading: 1 study, 2,132 students. i-Ready Classroom Mathematics: 1 multi-state quasi-experimental study, 31,192 students.

players.name: Kahoot!
players.what: Game-show quiz platform for classrooms, workplaces and homes, taken private in 2023 by a Goldman Sachs Asset Management consortium.
players.learner: K-12 classes first, plus corporate training and families
players.mechanism: Host projects multiple-choice questions, players answer on phones against a timer and a leaderboard
players.price: Teacher plans billed annually: Kahoot!+ Bronze $36 a year, Silver $84, Gold $144, Kahoot! One $228. Free Kahoot! Go tier. Player caps per game: 50, 100, 200, 800.

efficacy.finding: Academic achievement effect 0.772 (95% CI 0.540 to 1.004); retention effect 1.492. Effects this large from short classroom studies with researcher-made tests call for caution.
efficacy.design: Meta-analysis of 43 experimental studies, n=1,706 experimental and 1,647 control (Ozdemir 2025, Journal of Computer Assisted Learning).

players.name: Lexia (Core5, PowerUp)
players.what: Structured-literacy software for pre-K to grade 5 (Core5) and adolescents (PowerUp), part of Cambium Learning Group.
players.learner: Pre-K to grade 5 students, with a strand for struggling older readers; the buyer is the district
players.mechanism: Adaptive placement, then scaffolded phonics-to-comprehension activities that branch to guided practice or direct instruction on error, with teacher-led lessons flagged from the data

efficacy.finding: The disabilities trial reports an effect size of 0.24. Lexia's page claims 'ESSA Strong', effect sizes 'up to 0.53', and 40+ studies over 10 years. An Arizona Department of Education rubric lists the RAND study as ESSA Tier 2, moderate.
efficacy.design: Lexia-published research briefs. One randomized trial of students with reading and language-based disabilities: 3 schools (65 students) on Core5, 2 schools (50 students) business as usual. A separate 2021-22 grades 3 to 5 study run with RAND.

players.name: Moodle
players.what: Open-source learning management system that institutions host themselves or buy hosted from Moodle HQ and its partners.
players.learner: Universities, schools, and workplace training, strongest outside the US
players.mechanism: Course pages with activities, quizzes, forums, gradebook, and a plugin system

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Nearpod (Renaissance)
players.what: Interactive slide-lesson platform for K-12 teachers, bought by Renaissance in 2021 along with Flocabulary.
players.learner: K-12 students and teachers
players.mechanism: Teacher-paced or student-paced slide lessons with embedded polls, quizzes, drawing and video checks

efficacy.finding: Nearpod group outperformed control on reading comprehension and reading motivation. No effect size in the abstract.
efficacy.design: Experimental and control groups of EFL primary pupils, Nearpod with guided reading against regular teaching (Zahran 2025). The abstract states no sample size.

players.name: Newsela
players.what: Library of news and nonfiction articles rewritten at several reading levels for K-12 classrooms, with quizzes and writing prompts.
players.learner: Grade 2 to 12 students; the buyer is the school or district
players.mechanism: Each article is published at multiple Lexile levels with a short quiz; teachers assign by level

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: PowerSchool
players.what: K-12 student information system and school operations software, also owner of Schoology Learning; taken private by Bain Capital in 2024.
players.learner: District staff, teachers, parents and students
players.mechanism: System of record for enrollment, attendance, grades and scheduling, with LMS, assessment and analytics modules

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced. The one hit is unrelated.

players.name: Renaissance (Star, Accelerated Reader)
players.what: K-12 assessment and practice company: Star adaptive assessments, Accelerated Reader book quizzes, Freckle, and the Nearpod lesson platform.
players.learner: K-12 students; the buyer is the district
players.mechanism: Star places students with a short adaptive test; Accelerated Reader has students read a levelled book and pass a short comprehension quiz for points

efficacy.finding: Mixed effects on comprehension (grades 1 to 8) and no discernible effects on reading fluency (grades 3 to 5). For English language learners no study met standards.
efficacy.design: What Works Clearinghouse intervention report on Accelerated Reader, last updated June 2016; 2 of 11 eligible studies met standards

players.name: Schoology Learning (PowerSchool)
players.what: K-12 learning management system bought by PowerSchool in 2019 and sold alongside its student information system.
players.learner: K-12 students, teachers and parents; the buyer is the district
players.mechanism: Course pages, assignments, embedded formative assessment, gradebook sync with the PowerSchool SIS

efficacy.finding: Significant difference in learning outcome between the two conditions (p < 0.05); the abstract does not state the direction or size.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment, n=64 vocational high school students, blended learning on Schoology against problem-based learning (Irawan et al. 2017).

players.name: Seesaw
players.what: Elementary learning platform built around student digital portfolios and family sharing.
players.learner: Pre-K to grade 6 students, teachers and families
players.mechanism: Students post photos, drawings, audio and video of their work; teachers assign activities and families see the feed
players.price: Third-party aggregators conflict: Seesaw Plus at $120 a year per teacher with district licences per student (subger.com), and 'from $7 per pupil' (another aggregator). Seesaw's own pricing page was not opened.

efficacy.finding: No evaluation with a comparison group or a measured outcome surfaced.

players.name: Wayground (formerly Quizizz)
players.what: Gamified quiz and lesson platform for K-12 teachers; Quizizz renamed itself Wayground on 2025-06-24 and now calls itself a supplemental learning platform.
players.learner: K-12 students and teachers
players.mechanism: Self-paced or live quizzes with points and memes, plus a library of teacher-made resources
players.price: A free plan exists alongside paid options; no paid price was found.

efficacy.finding: Vocabulary recognition and retention rose 30.5% against 19.3% for control; eta squared 0.21 on picture identification; smaller gain on contextual use.
efficacy.design: Quasi-experiment on Quizizz, n=72 fourth graders in rural Taiwan (40 experimental, 32 control), ANCOVA on pre-test (Liu and Chen 2025).

players.name: Zearn
players.what: Nonprofit K-8 math program that pairs teacher-led small-group lessons with self-paced digital lessons.
players.learner: K-8 students; the buyer is the school or district
players.mechanism: Daily digital lesson with video instruction and scaffolded practice, alongside a full printed curriculum

efficacy.finding: Rated strong, average effect size +0.09. Texas trial: +0.11 on NWEA MAP (significant), +0.07 on STAAR (not significant). Louisiana: +0.20 on LEAP. The 2016-18 pilot found no significant difference.
efficacy.design: Evidence for ESSA review of 3 studies, 22,575 students. (1) RAND school-level randomized trial, 64 schools, over 10,000 students in grades 3 to 5, urban Texas district, 2022-24. (2) Johns Hopkins CRRE matched comparison, grades 4 to 8, three Louisiana districts, 2023-24. (3) Johns Hopkins CRRE matched pilot study, 2016-18.

players.name: AMBOSS

efficacy.finding: UWorld completion level was associated with Step 1 score (F(4,134)=10.29, p=.001). Students who finished the bank once or twice scored higher than those who did a few questions or half. In a regression with academic percentage, completion contributed B=6.52 (p=.001), model R squared .586. Prior academic performance was the strongest correlate (r=0.719). Number of practice exams had no effect (p=.663). Observational, so association only.
efficacy.design: Post-exam survey matched to Step 1 scores and preclinical grades, one Midwestern public medical school, classes of 2016 and 2017, 170 of 243 students (69.96 percent response). Published 2019 in Medical Science Educator.
